Thanks,
Daniel

text: After three years running the Saturday market stall, we have decided not to renew our pitch for next season. Rising rent (now $95 a week, up from $60) and the new parking charges mean we lose money most weekends. Our last market day will be 30 November. We will keep selling online and will offer free local delivery for orders over $40 until the end of the year. Thank you to everyone who came by, especially the regulars who have been with us since the first week.
notes: announcement: decision, reasons, last date, offer

text:
Incident report INC-2291

At 02:14 UTC the payments API started returning 503 errors for about 18% of requests. The on-call engineer, Tomasz, traced it to a database connection pool that was capped at 50 after Monday's config change. He raised the cap to 200 at 02:41 and errors stopped by 02:47. No payments were lost; 1,204 requests failed and were retried by clients. Action items: add an alert on pool usage above 80% (owner: Grace, due Friday), and require a second reviewer for config changes (owner: Tomasz).
notes: incident report: cause, fix, impact, owners

Hello parents,

The Year 5 trip to the science museum is on Wednesday 9 October. Children must be at school by 8:15 as the coach leaves at 8:30 sharp. Please send a packed lunch in a disposable bag, a water bottle and a coat. No money is needed. The trip costs £12, which can be paid on the school app until Friday 4 October. If your child gets travel sick, let the class teacher know and give them their medicine in the morning. We will be back at about 3:30.

text: I've looked at both quotes for the kitchen. Builder A is £18,500 and can start on 1 April, but their reviews mention delays. Builder B is £21,000, starts in June, and includes the electrics, which A charges £2,200 extra for. So the real difference is only £300. My vote is B, mainly for the electrics and the reviews, but I'm fine with A if you'd rather start sooner. We need to tell them by the end of next week.
